import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

data = {
    'Year': [2018, 2018, 2018, 2019, 2019, 2019, 2020, 2020, 2020, 2021, 2021, 2021],
    'Region': [
        'Sub-Saharan Africa', 'South Asia', 'Latin America & Caribbean',
        'Sub-Saharan Africa', 'South Asia', 'Latin America & Caribbean',
        'Sub-Saharan Africa', 'South Asia', 'Latin America & Caribbean',
        'Sub-Saharan Africa', 'South Asia', 'Latin America & Caribbean'
    ],
    'ODA_Percentage': [2.9, 4.2, 0.7, 2.4, 3.9, -0.1, -2.1, -5.6, -7.0, 3.7, 7.2, 3.1],
    'GDP_Growth': [45.2, 28.9, 25.9, 48.7, 30.4, 20.9, 52.1, 29.6, 18.3, 54.2, 31.5, 17.8]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(10, 10), sharex=True)

sns.lineplot(
    data=df,
    x='Year',
    y='ODA_Percentage',
    hue='Region',
    style='Region',
    markers=True,
    dashes=False,
    palette='viridis',
    ax=axes[0]
)
axes[0].set_title('Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) as % of Gross Capital Formation')
axes[0].set_ylabel('GDP Growth (%)')
axes[0].grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)
axes[0].legend(title='Region', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

sns.lineplot(
    data=df,
    x='Year',
    y='GDP_Growth',
    hue='Region',
    style='Region',
    markers=True,
    dashes=False,
    palette='viridis',
    ax=axes[1]
)
axes[1].set_title('GDP Growth Rate by Region')
axes[1].set_ylabel('GDP Growth (%)')
axes[1].set_xlabel('Year')
axes[1].grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)
axes[1].legend(title='Region', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
===== summary.txt
The image presents a multi-axes line chart that compares Official Development Assistance (ODA) as a percentage of Gross Capital Formation and GDP growth rates across three regions: Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and Latin America & Caribbean from 2018 to 2021.

The first chart, titled "Official Development Assistance (ODA) as % of Gross Capital Formation," displays ODA percentages on the vertical axis, ranging from 15% to 55%. The horizontal axis represents the years from 2018 to 2021. Three distinct lines, each marked with different symbols, represent the regions. Sub-Saharan Africa is depicted with a dark blue line and circular markers, showing a steady increase from 45.2% in 2018 to 54.2% in 2021. South Asia, represented by a teal line with "x" markers, shows a slight fluctuation, starting at 28.9% in 2018, peaking at 30.4% in 2019, and reaching 31.5% in 2021. Latin America & Caribbean is illustrated with a light green line and square markers, displaying a decline from 25.9% in 2018 to 17.8% in 2021.

The second chart, titled "GDP Growth Rate by Region," presents GDP growth percentages on the vertical axis, ranging from -7% to 7%. The same three regions are depicted with the same color schemes and markers as in the first chart. Sub-Saharan Africa's GDP growth, shown by the dark blue line, starts at 2.9% in 2018, dips to 2.4% in 2019, further declines to -2.1% in 2020, and then recovers to 3.7% in 2021. South Asia, represented by the teal line, begins at 4.2% in 2018, drops to 3.9% in 2019, plunges to -5.6% in 2020, and significantly rebounds to 7.2% in 2021. Latin America & Caribbean, indicated by the light green line, starts at 0.7% in 2018, decreases to -0.1% in 2019, reaches a low of -7.0% in 2020, and then rises to 3.1% in 2021.

Both charts feature grid lines for easier readability and include a legend to distinguish the regions clearly. The overall design provides a clear and comparative view of how ODA and GDP growth rates have evolved over the specified years for each region.
